findings.issue_text: Copy-pasted null check in AccessTokenContext.java:76-77 re-validates grantType instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is silently accepted and produces token IDs ending in ':null' (e.g. 'onrtac:null'), which would silently create colliding token IDs since the raw ID is the uniqueness-bearing part of the jti

isAccessTokenId matcher in AssertEvents.java:480-484 has a wrong offset (reads substring(3,5) instead of substring(4,6) where the grant shortcut actually is) and inverted comparison logic (returns false on equality), making the grant-type assertions in expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken and expectAuthReqIdToToken vacuous so grant-encoding regressions go undetected; additionally substring(3,5) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for prefixes shorter than 5 chars

OAuth2GrantType.java:102 vs 108: grantType is captured from formParams only in the constructor, while the pre-existing setFormParams() replaces formParams without recomputing grantType, so context.getGrantType() returns a stale value that createTokenResponse bakes into the token's encoded ID

Inconsistent grant labeling: LegacyTokenExchangeProvider (legacy token-exchange path) and possibly UMA PermissionGrantType issue access tokens via TokenManager.createClientAccessToken without setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE, so those tokens are encoded with the 'na' placeholder grant, making the same logical grant produce different encoded contexts depending on code path and undermining reliability of getTokenContextFromTokenId

AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic (returns false when the extracted grant shortcut equals the expected one) and wrong substring offsets (uses substring(3,5) instead of substring(4,6)), making the grant-type assertion vacuous - it passes for any grant type, so expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, and expectAuthReqIdToToken have effectively no grant-type regression coverage

AccessTokenContext constructor has a copy-pasted null check: the second Objects.requireNonNull re-validates grantType instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId passes validation and silently produces malformed token IDs like 'onrtac:null' that fail decode round-trips

OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc says the shortcut is 'usually like 3-letters' but the encoder requires exactly 2-char shortcuts (getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-fails with 'Expected length of 6' otherwise), and postInit only validates duplicate shortcuts, never shortcut format/length, so a custom 3-char shortcut would produce token IDs that cannot be decoded and would not be caught at startup

Cache-miss paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut re-scan grant factories on every call with no negative caching, so failed lookups repeat on every subsequent miss; if decode lands on an attacker-facing hot path, add negative caching

isAccessTokenId matcher in AssertEvents.java is vacuous: the condition polarity is inverted (a match returns no-match) and the offset is wrong — substring(3, 5) should be substring(4, 6) to capture the grant shortcut, so the matcher only asserts the prefix:UUID shape and tokens with any grant type pass

Copy-paste bug in AccessTokenContext.java: the second Objects.requireNonNull checks grantType again instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId passes validation and later produces malformed IDs like 'onrtac:null' instead of failing fast

testIncorrectGrantType passes for the wrong reason: before() calls only init(null) and never postInit, so sessionFactory is null and decoding 'ofrtac:5678' NPEs at sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...), which the broad catch(RuntimeException) swallows — the test is green due to an NPE rather than the intended IllegalArgumentException validation path and masks regressions in unknown-shortcut validation
AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId grant assertion uses wrong offset: substring(3, 5) should be substring(4, 6) since the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5 in the st(2)+tt(2)+gs(2) encoded context

AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId has inverted logic: `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects matches instead of requiring them (!equals was intended), making the matcher pass any <6 chars>:<uuid> regardless of grant shortcut

OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() added as a new abstract SPI method with no default implementation, causing AbstractMethodError and potential server startup failure for third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations compiled against the previous interface

Externally visible token-ID (jti) / event token_id format changed from raw UUID to ssttgg:<uuid> (leaking into access token JWT jti claim, introspection response, and event schema) without opt-out, encoder selection guidance, or migration note for external consumers

Shortcut length contract is self-contradictory: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory javadoc invites 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but the decoder hard-requires exactly 2 chars (encodedContext.length() != 6 throws IllegalArgumentException), and neither encodeTokenId nor postInit validates shortcut length, so custom grants can issue token IDs that cannot be decoded

Copy-paste bug in AccessTokenContext constructor: the second Objects.requireNonNull checks grantType again instead of rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId to silently produce token IDs like 'onrtac:null'

Public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) removed without replacement, breaking external callers/forks at compile time (or NoSuchMethodError if precompiled) with no migration path provided

Context.grantType is derived only in the constructor; setFormParams() replaces formParams without recomputing grantType, leaving getGrantType() stale and inconsistent with getFormParams() for callers that swap form params after construction

Incomplete caller updates for the new token_id event format: only 4 helper expectations (code, device, refresh, CIBA) were updated, but Details.TOKEN_ID carries the encoded format for every grant routing through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse (password, client credentials, UMA/permission, pre-authorized code, token exchange), so remaining test expectations asserting a plain UUID will fail

Copy-paste bug in AccessTokenContext constructor: the fourth Objects.requireNonNull re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId passes validation silently and would flow through encodeTokenId producing a malformed jti ('onrtac:null'); the misleading 'Null grantType not allowed' message would also misdirect debugging
AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId test matcher has inverted logic: it returns false (mismatch) when the extracted grant shortcut equals the expected shortcut, instead of when it differs

AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId test matcher uses wrong substring offsets: substring(3, 5) reads the last char of tokenType plus the first char of grantType rather than the 2-char grant shortcut (positions 4-5), so the matcher can never match in practice and silently passes for any 6-char prefix + UUID, making all grant-encoding event assertions in the PR (expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectAuthReqIdToToken) verify nothing
AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId test matcher has a latent StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: substring(3, 5) throws for prefixes of 3-4 chars instead of returning a clean mismatch

No validation that grant shortcuts are exactly 2 chars (or colon-free) in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, and the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', contradicting the hard-coded 6-char (2+2+2) wire format; a provider returning a 3-char shortcut would encode token IDs that can never be decoded, deferring failure from registration time to token-handling time

New required abstract getShortcut() on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks binary compatibility: precompiled third-party grant providers throw AbstractMethodError during postInit (server fails to start), and a provider returning null triggers an NPE from ConcurrentHashMap.put

Removed public copy constructor Context(Context) from OAuth2GrantType.Context is a binary-breaking SPI change: external providers compiled against the old class will get NoSuchMethodError at request time after upgrade, with no deprecation or compile-time warning

getTokenContextFromTokenId throws unchecked IllegalArgumentException on malformed token IDs (wrong-length prefixes, unknown shortcuts) with no caller contract or wrapping; once wired into request paths, crafted or legacy-malformed token IDs would surface as unhandled exceptions/500s unless every caller remembers to catch it

isAccessTokenId matcher extracts substring at wrong indices (3-4 instead of 4-5 for the grant shortcut) and inverts the comparison logic, so it accepts any grant shortcut instead of verifying the expected one, providing zero regression protection for the grant-type portion of the encoding
isAccessTokenId matcher would throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for a token ID prefix shorter than 5 chars instead of failing cleanly
getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the core derivation logic (TRANSIENT vs OFFLINE vs ONLINE detection, lightweight-vs-regular, 'na' fallback) — has no test coverage at any layer

Unit test bypasses postInit and hand-crafts factory internals with only two grants, leaving the real wiring of ~9 grant shortcuts, the duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException guard, and the lazy map-refresh fallbacks in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut untested

No end-to-end assertion that issued token IDs encode the correct session type ('of', 'tr') or token type ('lt'); the only integration format assertion checks merely 'something:uuid', so context encoding is never verified against a token produced by an actual flow
testIncorrectGrantType catches broad RuntimeException instead of asserting the specific IllegalArgumentException, and the caught variable is unused
Untested error branches in getTokenContextFromTokenId: prefix length ≠ 6, unknown session-type shortcut, unknown token-type shortcut, IDs with more than one colon, and empty rawId

Context.grantType is captured only at construction; setFormParams replaces formParams without refreshing grantType, so createTokenResponse could stamp a stale grant type if a flow swaps form params after construction (low confidence, might be a false positive)

AssertEvents.java:482 grant-shortcut assertion is vacuous due to two canceling bugs: substring(3,5) uses wrong indices (shortcut actually at substring(4,6)) and the condition is inverted (returns false on equality), so expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken assert nothing about grant type and a token with the wrong grant would pass
AssertEvents.java:482 substring(3,5) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException (rather than returning a clean false) for token-ID prefixes shorter than 5 chars

OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc blesses a 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider hardcodes exactly 2 chars per component and rejects anything else (encodedContext.length() != 6 -> IllegalArgumentException), so implementations following the documented guidance produce token IDs that encode fine but can never be decoded; the javadoc should mandate exactly 2 chars and postInit should enforce it

AccessTokenContext.java:78-79 copy-paste bug: the second Objects.requireNonNull re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId passes validation and silently yields IDs like 'onrtna:null'

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.testIncorrectGrantType passes for the wrong reason: before() never calls postInit so factory.sessionFactory is null, decoding 'ofrtac:5678' misses the shortcut and NPEs in getGrantTypeByShortcut, and the broad catch(RuntimeException) swallows the NPE — the test would also pass if the IllegalArgumentException validation were removed entirely; assert the specific exception type and initialize/stub sessionFactory

Grant-type attribution is scattered across five sites (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType, TokenManager.validateToken refresh path, StandardTokenExchangeProvider) with redundant manual sets of the same value createTokenResponse would set; the implicit convention means any future token-issuing path that forgets to set Constants.GRANT_TYPE degrades quietly to 'na' with no error — centralize the derivation or drop the redundant sets

Layering leak: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider depends on the protocol-mapper internal AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken (widened from package-private to public static, a source-compat change for mapper subclasses), and that method reads the ambient session.getContext().getClient() rather than the client whose token is being created, which could diverge (e.g., token-exchange target client) and bake a wrong token-type marker into the ID; the policy should live in its own concern taking the client explicitly

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId is a speculative decode path with no production caller (tests only), and the lazy 'refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' fallbacks in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut handle a scenario that cannot occur (providers are fixed at startup and postInit runs after all factories load) while side-effecting shared maps from read paths; trim until needed or wire the consumer immediately

OAuth2GrantType.setFormParams replaces this.formParams without re-deriving grantType (captured once in the constructor), leaving the context internally inconsistent with a stale or null grantType alongside fresh params; derive grantType lazily or update it in the setter

Removal of the public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) is a silent source-compat break for external grant-type extensions that copied contexts, even though no in-repo callers remain; worth a release-notes mention or a deprecated-then-removed cycle

Magic string 'na' (UNKNOWN) conflates the encoded 2-char shortcut with the decoded grant-type domain value: AccessTokenContext.getGrantType() returns the literal 'na' when the grant was unrecorded, forcing callers to compare against the encoder impl's constant to detect unknown; use a sentinel on AccessTokenContext or a nullable grantType to keep the wire format out of the domain model

isAccessTokenId test matcher in AssertEvents.java (line 483) uses wrong substring offsets: the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5 of the encoded ID (e.g. 'onrtac:...'), so substring(3, 5) should be substring(4, 6); the current code extracts the 2nd char of the token-type shortcut plus the 1st char of the grant shortcut (e.g. 'ta' for 'onrtac')

isAccessTokenId test matcher has inverted polarity: it returns false (matcher fails) when the extracted pair equals the expected grant shortcut and proceeds to the UUID check when it does not, which is exactly backwards

Net effect of the matcher bugs: isAccessTokenId degenerates to a 'one colon + UUID tail' check that passes regardless of which grant shortcut the encoder emitted, so the four updated expectations (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) verify none of the per-grant encoding and a regression emitting wrong grant shortcuts stays green (silent-pass guard)
Latent spurious-failure in isAccessTokenId: an expected 'rt' shortcut matches chars 3-4 of a regular token ID from the token-exchange grant ('onrtte:...' -> 'rt'), causing false negatives
substring(3, 5) in isAccessTokenId throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for any ID prefix shorter than 5 chars

Grant-shortcut contract mismatch: getShortcut() javadoc invites a '3-letters shortcut' but the decoder (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:76) hard-requires a 6-char context (2+2+2) and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise; all built-in shortcuts are 2 chars so the mismatch is invisible to in-repo tests

encodeTokenId (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:105-118) performs no length, charset, or collision validation of the shortcut: a custom grant factory following the javadoc (e.g. 'abc') produces IDs like 'onrtabc:uuid' that encode successfully but can never be decoded (encode/decode asymmetry surfacing at decode time), and a shortcut containing ':' corrupts the colon-split entirely
postInit duplicate-shortcut validation is only a size comparison (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()), which detects some but not all shortcut collisions

Lazy registration paths in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:110-137) put into the shared maps with no collision check, bypassing postInit validation entirely; a lazily registered colliding shortcut silently overwrites the previous mapping, so previously issued tokens decode as the wrong grant type

AccessTokenContext constructor (lines 79-80) has a copy-pasted requireNonNull: the second line checks grantType again instead of rawTokenId, so rawTokenId is never null-checked; a null rawTokenId flows through and yields token IDs like 'onrtna:null'

testIncorrectGrantType (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:95-104) passes via incidental NPE rather than the intended validation: the test factory never runs postInit so sessionFactory is null and decoding 'ofrtac:5678' NPEs inside getGrantTypeByShortcut; even if the shortcut validation were deleted the test would still pass (NPE from requireNonNull(grantType) in AccessTokenContext), and catch(RuntimeException) swallows both, so the test cannot detect removal of the decode validation

adjudication.rationale: In OAuth2GrantType.Context, the new field `grantType` is initialized only once in the constructor from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`. The existing mutator `setFormParams(MultivaluedHashMap<String, String> formParams)` still exists but (as shown in the diff) there is no corresponding recomputation/update of `grantType` when `formParams` is replaced. Since `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse(...)` now persists `context.getGrantType()` into `clientSessionCtx` (`clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())`), a stale `grantType` would be baked into the token context/encoded token ID if `setFormParams()` is used after construction.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple code paths explicitly setting `clientSessionCtx/sessionContext` attribute `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` (e.g., `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`, `StandardTokenExchangeProvider`, refresh handling in `TokenManager`, `PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType`, `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType`). Therefore the claim is not grounded in the provided changes.

Cache-miss paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut re-scan grant factories on every call with no negative caching, so failed lookups repeat on every subsequent miss; if decode lands on an attacker-facing hot path, add negative caching

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, both miss paths do extra work but don’t record the miss: getShortcutByGrantType() calls sessionFactory.getProviderFactory(...) when grantsToShortcuts.get(grantType) is null, and if that returns null nothing is stored, so subsequent calls for the same unknown grantType repeat the lookup. Similarly, getGrantTypeByShortcut() scans sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class) when grantsByShortcuts.get(shortcut) is null, and if not found it stores nothing, so subsequent calls for the same unknown shortcut repeat the scan. This is a diff-grounded performance/DoS-hardening concern rather than a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId matcher in AssertEvents.java is vacuous: the condition polarity is inverted (a match returns no-match) and the offset is wrong — substring(3, 5) should be substring(4, 6) to capture the grant shortcut, so the matcher only asserts the prefix:UUID shape and tokens with any grant type pass

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the match logic is incorrect: it returns false when the extracted substring equals the expected grant shortcut (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), which inverts the intended polarity. Additionally, given the encoded prefix format elsewhere in the diff (2 chars sessionType + 2 chars tokenType + 2 chars grantShortcut, total 6), the grant shortcut should be at indices [4,6), not [3,5). As written, the matcher effectively only validates the `prefix:UUID` shape (and may even reject correct values if the buggy substring happens to equal), allowing tokens with any grant type to pass.

adjudication.rationale: In `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the 4th validation line is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This means `rawTokenId` can be null without failing fast, and later `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, producing IDs ending in `:null` rather than throwing early.

adjudication.rationale: In the new access token id encoding, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId()` explicitly treats the encoded context as 6 chars with grant shortcut in the last two chars: `gtShortcut = encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`. However, the newly added test matcher `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId()` checks `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, which spans the last char of tokenType and first char of grantType, so it will not correctly validate the grant shortcut position for the `st(2)+tt(2)+gs(2)` format.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the matcher rejects the expected grant shortcut: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` inverts the intended condition (it should fail when it does NOT equal). As written, it will accept token IDs whose parsed shortcut differs from `expectedGrantShortcut`, so the grant shortcut is not actually enforced by the matcher.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() added as a new abstract SPI method with no default implementation, causing AbstractMethodError and potential server startup failure for third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations compiled against the previous interface

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default implementation. Existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations compiled against the previous interface would not contain this method; when Keycloak calls it, it would trigger `AbstractMethodError`. This call is made unconditionally during startup in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` via `gtf.getShortcut()`, so such providers could cause server startup failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Externally visible token-ID (jti) / event token_id format changed from raw UUID to ssttgg:<uuid> (leaking into access token JWT jti claim, introspection response, and event schema) without opt-out, encoder selection guidance, or migration note for external consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes the access token `jti`/token id generation from a raw UUID to an encoded form `ssttgg:<rawId>`: `TokenManager.initToken()` no longer does `token.id(generateId())` and instead builds an `AccessTokenContext` and calls `encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)` (services/.../TokenManager.java). The default encoder (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId`) prefixes 6 chars (session type + token type + grant shortcut) and a `:` before the raw id. Tests were updated to expect this new format for `Details.TOKEN_ID` (AssertEvents.java), confirming this is intended and externally observable (events). The finding’s concerns about breaking external consumers/migration/opt-out are diff-grounded as an architectural/compatibility issue (no toggle or alternate path is shown in the diff), but it’s not a verifiable correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Shortcut length contract is self-contradictory: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory javadoc invites 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but the decoder hard-requires exactly 2 chars (encodedContext.length() != 6 throws IllegalArgumentException), and neither encodeTokenId nor postInit validates shortcut length, so custom grants can issue token IDs that cannot be decoded

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a hard 2-character shortcut encoding/decoding scheme for grant type in access token IDs: `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` concatenates `sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grantShort+':'+rawId`, while `getTokenContextFromTokenId` enforces `encodedContext.length() == 6` and slices grant shortcut as `substring(4, 6)`, i.e., exactly 2 chars. However, `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory#getShortcut()` javadoc says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", and neither `postInit` nor `encodeTokenId` validates that `getShortcut()` returns exactly 2 characters. Therefore a custom/third-party grant factory returning a 3-char shortcut (as suggested by the javadoc) could successfully encode token IDs that will always fail decoding with `IllegalArgumentException`, which is a real behavioral defect exposed by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Copy-paste bug in AccessTokenContext constructor: the second Objects.requireNonNull checks grantType again instead of rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId to silently produce token IDs like 'onrtac:null'

adjudication.rationale: In `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the null-check intended for `rawTokenId` is a copy-paste error: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId` (new file `services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java`). This allows `rawTokenId` to be null without failing fast, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` would then concatenate `":" + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()` producing an encoded token id ending with `:null`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) removed without replacement, breaking external callers/forks at compile time (or NoSuchMethodError if precompiled) with no migration path provided

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context` (it existed and is deleted with no alternative constructor/method added to clone/copy a Context). This is an API/ABI compatibility break for any external code that used that public constructor, potentially causing compile errors or `NoSuchMethodError` for previously compiled extensions. The diff itself doesn’t show a migration path or replacement for copying contexts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Context.grantType is derived only in the constructor; setFormParams() replaces formParams without recomputing grantType, leaving getGrantType() stale and inconsistent with getFormParams() for callers that swap form params after construction

adjudication.rationale: In OAuth2GrantType.Context, a new field `grantType` is initialized once in the constructor from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)` (line adding `this.grantType = ...`). However, `setFormParams(MultivaluedHashMap<String, String> formParams)` still replaces `this.formParams` without updating `this.grantType`. Since a public `getGrantType()` accessor was added and other code now uses it (e.g., `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` sets `clientSessionCtx` attribute from `context.getGrantType()`), any caller that invokes `setFormParams()` after construction will observe `getFormParams()` and `getGrantType()` becoming inconsistent, yielding stale/incorrect grant type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Incomplete caller updates for the new token_id event format: only 4 helper expectations (code, device, refresh, CIBA) were updated, but Details.TOKEN_ID carries the encoded format for every grant routing through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse (password, client credentials, UMA/permission, pre-authorized code, token exchange), so remaining test expectations asserting a plain UUID will fail

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that access token IDs are now encoded (TokenManager.initToken uses TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId), and AssertEvents was updated for 4 event helpers to stop expecting a plain UUID. However, the finding’s core claim—"remaining test expectations asserting a plain UUID will fail" for other grants (password, client credentials, UMA, pre-authorized code, token exchange)—cannot be verified from this diff because no other expectations/callers asserting Details.TOKEN_ID == UUID are shown. The statement about incomplete updates across the rest of the testsuite is therefore not provable from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Copy-paste bug in AccessTokenContext constructor: the fourth Objects.requireNonNull re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId passes validation silently and would flow through encodeTokenId producing a malformed jti ('onrtac:null'); the misleading 'Null grantType not allowed' message would also misdirect debugging

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the fourth null-check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This means `rawTokenId` can be null without triggering validation, and the error message is also misleading. The diff also shows `encodeTokenId` appends `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which would yield a token id ending in `:null` if `rawTokenId` is null.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId test matcher has inverted logic: it returns false (mismatch) when the extracted grant shortcut equals the expected shortcut, instead of when it differs

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, matchesSafely() does `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, which rejects the case where the extracted grant shortcut equals the expected one and accepts mismatching shortcuts (as long as the raw id part is a UUID). This is inverted comparison logic relative to the intended matcher behavior described in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId test matcher uses wrong substring offsets: substring(3, 5) reads the last char of tokenType plus the first char of grantType rather than the 2-char grant shortcut (positions 4-5), so the matcher can never match in practice and silently passes for any 6-char prefix + UUID, making all grant-encoding event assertions in the PR (expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectAuthReqIdToToken) verify nothing

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the grant shortcut is incorrectly extracted and checked. The encoded prefix is 6 chars (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grantType), so the grant shortcut should be items[0].substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5) which spans the last char of tokenType and first char of grantType. Additionally, the logic is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects matches instead of accepting them. As written, the matcher will typically return true for tokens with any prefix (as long as substring(3,5) != expected) plus a UUID raw id, so the new event assertions largely don’t validate the intended grant encoding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId test matcher has a latent StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: substring(3, 5) throws for prefixes of 3-4 chars instead of returning a clean mismatch

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, after splitting on ':', it unconditionally does `items[0].substring(3, 5)` without checking `items[0].length() >= 5`. For any token id string of the form "<shortPrefix>:<uuid>" where `<shortPrefix>` is shorter than 5 characters, this matcher will throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning `false` (clean mismatch). The diff shows no guard for that condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No validation that grant shortcuts are exactly 2 chars (or colon-free) in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, and the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', contradicting the hard-coded 6-char (2+2+2) wire format; a provider returning a 3-char shortcut would encode token IDs that can never be decoded, deferring failure from registration time to token-handling time

adjudication.rationale: The diff hard-codes a 6-character encoded context (2 chars sessionType + 2 chars tokenType + 2 chars grantType) in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(): it throws if encodedContext.length() != 6 and then slices fixed substrings (0,2),(2,4),(4,6). However, OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()’s new javadoc says shortcuts are “usually like 3-letters”, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() registers whatever shortcut implementations return with no validation of length==2 or absence of ':' characters. As a result, a grant implementation returning a 3-character (or colon-containing) shortcut could produce token IDs via encodeTokenId() that cannot be decoded (or are split incorrectly), shifting failure to token parsing time rather than registration/init time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New required abstract getShortcut() on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks binary compatibility: precompiled third-party grant providers throw AbstractMethodError during postInit (server fails to start), and a provider returning null triggers an NPE from ConcurrentHashMap.put

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the public SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` and then unconditionally calls it during startup in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` (`String grantShortcut = gtf.getShortcut();`). Any precompiled third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation built against the old interface will not have this method, leading to `AbstractMethodError` at runtime when `postInit()` invokes it. Additionally, `postInit()` stores the shortcut into `ConcurrentHashMap` via `grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName);`; if an implementation returns `null` for the shortcut, `ConcurrentHashMap.put` throws `NullPointerException`, causing startup failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed public copy constructor Context(Context) from OAuth2GrantType.Context is a binary-breaking SPI change: external providers compiled against the old class will get NoSuchMethodError at request time after upgrade, with no deprecation or compile-time warning

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the public copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` from `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context` (server-spi-private). Any external OAuth2 grant provider compiled against that constructor would hit a binary incompatibility after upgrade (e.g., `NoSuchMethodError` when invoking it), and the diff shows no deprecation/shim to preserve compatibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws unchecked IllegalArgumentException on malformed token IDs (wrong-length prefixes, unknown shortcuts) with no caller contract or wrapping; once wired into request paths, crafted or legacy-malformed token IDs would surface as unhandled exceptions/500s unless every caller remembers to catch it

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromTokenId, malformed/unknown encodings do throw unchecked IllegalArgumentException (encodedContext.length()!=6; unknown session/token/grant shortcuts), while TokenContextEncoderProvider has no documented contract about exceptions vs. returning UNKNOWN. However, within this diff there is no wiring/usage of getTokenContextFromTokenId in request paths (TokenManager only encodes token IDs), so the claim about unhandled 500s being exposed by this PR is speculative based solely on the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId matcher extracts substring at wrong indices (3-4 instead of 4-5 for the grant shortcut) and inverts the comparison logic, so it accepts any grant shortcut instead of verifying the expected one, providing zero regression protection for the grant-type portion of the encoding

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the grant-type shortcut check is both indexed and logically wrong. The token-id context prefix is encoded as 6 chars (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grantType), so the grant shortcut should be extracted with substring(4, 6), but the code uses items[0].substring(3, 5). Additionally, it inverts the comparison: `if ( ... .equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the expected shortcut and accepts any other shortcut as long as the raw id part is a UUID, so it provides no regression protection for the encoded grant-type portion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId matcher would throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for a token ID prefix shorter than 5 chars instead of failing cleanly

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, matchesSafely does `items[0].substring(3, 5)` after only checking `items.length != 2`. If the token id has exactly one ':' but the prefix before ':' is shorter than 5 characters (e.g. `"ab:..."`), `substring(3,5)` will throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException rather than returning `false`. The diff shows no length guard on `items[0]`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the core derivation logic (TRANSIENT vs OFFLINE vs ONLINE detection, lightweight-vs-regular, 'na' fallback) — has no test coverage at any layer

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial derivation logic in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)` (session persistence/offline → `SessionType`, `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)` → `TokenType`, and `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` with `UNKNOWN` fallback). The only new test file `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` exercises `getTokenContextFromTokenId(...)` and `encodeTokenId(...)` using a `null` session/provider context, and does not cover `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)` at all. No other added tests in the diff appear to validate that derivation path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unit test bypasses postInit and hand-crafts factory internals with only two grants, leaving the real wiring of ~9 grant shortcuts, the duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException guard, and the lazy map-refresh fallbacks in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut untested

adjudication.rationale: The new unit test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` explicitly bypasses `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(...)` and instead directly assigns `factory.grantsByShortcuts` / `factory.grantsToShortcuts` with only `ro`, `cc`, and `na` (UNKNOWN). Therefore it does not exercise the real production wiring done in `postInit` (iterating all `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations and populating ~multiple grant shortcuts), does not cover the duplicate-shortcut/ID guard (`if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()) throw ...`), and cannot cover the lazy refresh logic in `getShortcutByGrantType` / `getGrantTypeByShortcut` (which depends on `sessionFactory`, not set in the test). This is a concrete test coverage gap for the newly added factory logic, not a runtime defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No end-to-end assertion that issued token IDs encode the correct session type ('of', 'tr') or token type ('lt'); the only integration format assertion checks merely 'something:uuid', so context encoding is never verified against a token produced by an actual flow

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces token-id context encoding (6-char prefix: 2 for session type, 2 for token type, 2 for grant shortcut) via `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)` and uses it in `TokenManager.initToken()` to set `token.id(...)`. However, the only integration-level assertions added in `AssertEvents` validate the token id using `isAccessTokenId(...)`, which merely checks the overall `prefix:uuid` shape and (attempts to) check the grant shortcut, but does not assert the session type (`on/of/tr`) or token type (`rt/lt`) portions of the prefix. Unit tests (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest`) cover encode/decode logic, but there is no end-to-end assertion against a real flow-produced token that verifies those session/token-type bits are correctly encoded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testIncorrectGrantType catches broad RuntimeException instead of asserting the specific IllegalArgumentException, and the caught variable is unused
matched_golden_ids: Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that the test is catching a too-broad RuntimeException when the code under test throws IllegalArgumentException, so the test should assert/catch the specific exception type for precision. The candidate adds an extra note about the unused variable, but the core issue matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Untested error branches in getTokenContextFromTokenId: prefix length ≠ 6, unknown session-type shortcut, unknown token-type shortcut, IDs with more than one colon, and empty rawId

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new parsing/validation logic in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId (length check `encodedContext.length() != 6` and IllegalArgumentException branches for unknown sessionType/tokenType/grantType shortcuts). The added unit test DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest covers: valid cases, unknown grant type shortcut (`na`), old token without colon, and one incorrect grant type shortcut. It does not exercise several explicit error/edge branches now present in the new code: prefix length ≠ 6 (throws), unknown session-type shortcut (throws), unknown token-type shortcut (throws), and cases like additional colons or empty rawId are not validated and not tested. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap for newly introduced nontrivial parsing behavior, but not a demonstrable correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Context.grantType is captured only at construction; setFormParams replaces formParams without refreshing grantType, so createTokenResponse could stamp a stale grant type if a flow swaps form params after construction (low confidence, might be a false positive)

adjudication.rationale: In OAuth2GrantType.Context, `grantType` is derived from `formParams` only in the constructor (`this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);`). The class still exposes `setFormParams(...)` which replaces `this.formParams` but does not recompute `grantType`, so `getGrantType()` can return a value inconsistent with the current `formParams`. Since later code stamps `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` (e.g., in `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`), this can propagate a stale grant type if `setFormParams` is used after construction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.java:482 grant-shortcut assertion is vacuous due to two canceling bugs: substring(3,5) uses wrong indices (shortcut actually at substring(4,6)) and the condition is inverted (returns false on equality), so expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken assert nothing about grant type and a token with the wrong grant would pass

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), the grant shortcut position is miscomputed and the match condition is inverted. Token IDs are encoded as 6-char context (2 session + 2 token + 2 grant) + ':' + UUID (see DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId), so the grant shortcut is at substring(4,6), not substring(3,5). Additionally, matchesSafely returns false when the extracted substring equals expectedGrantShortcut (`if (...) return false;`), meaning it only checks that the UUID part matches and effectively does not assert the expected grant type; tokens with the wrong grant shortcut will pass these expectations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.java:482 substring(3,5) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException (rather than returning a clean false) for token-ID prefixes shorter than 5 chars

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId (added in this diff), matchesSafely() calls items[0].substring(3, 5) without checking items[0].length() >= 5. If a token ID contains ':' but has a shorter prefix (e.g., "a:uuid"), this will throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc blesses a 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider hardcodes exactly 2 chars per component and rejects anything else (encodedContext.length() != 6 -> IllegalArgumentException), so implementations following the documented guidance produce token IDs that encode fine but can never be decoded; the javadoc should mandate exactly 2 chars and postInit should enforce it
matched_golden_ids: Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out a documentation/implementation mismatch around shortcut length: Javadoc suggests ~3-letter shortcuts, while actual usage/decoding assumes 2-letter components (e.g., hardcoded 6-length encoded context). Candidate adds extra detail about decoding failure and enforcement, but the core issue (docs should reflect 2-letter pattern) matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext.java:78-79 copy-paste bug: the second Objects.requireNonNull re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId passes validation and silently yields IDs like 'onrtna:null'

adjudication.rationale: In `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the 4th null-check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This means `rawTokenId` can be null without validation, and later `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, yielding an encoded ID containing `null` (e.g., `...:null`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.testIncorrectGrantType passes for the wrong reason: before() never calls postInit so factory.sessionFactory is null, decoding 'ofrtac:5678' misses the shortcut and NPEs in getGrantTypeByShortcut, and the broad catch(RuntimeException) swallows the NPE — the test would also pass if the IllegalArgumentException validation were removed entirely; assert the specific exception type and initialize/stub sessionFactory

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before(), the factory only calls init(null) and manually seeds grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts; it never calls postInit(), so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.sessionFactory remains null. In getTokenContextFromTokenId("ofrtac:5678"), gtShortcut="ac" is missing, so getGrantTypeByShortcut() falls into the refresh branch and dereferences sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...), causing an NPE. testIncorrectGrantType catches any RuntimeException, so it would pass even if the intended IllegalArgumentException validation logic changed/was removed. This is a real, diff-grounded test weakness rather than a production defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Grant-type attribution is scattered across five sites (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType, TokenManager.validateToken refresh path, StandardTokenExchangeProvider) with redundant manual sets of the same value createTokenResponse would set; the implicit convention means any future token-issuing path that forgets to set Constants.GRANT_TYPE degrades quietly to 'na' with no error — centralize the derivation or drop the redundant sets

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new convention that access-token IDs encode the grant type via `ClientSessionContext` attribute `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` (see `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`, which falls back to `UNKNOWN`/"na" when the attribute is missing). The attribute is set in multiple places: `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` (central), plus explicit sets in `PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType`, `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType`, `TokenManager.validateToken` (refresh path), and `StandardTokenExchangeProvider`. This scattering is verifiable in the diff and means any token-issuing path that forgets to set the attribute will silently encode grant type as "na" rather than failing, which is an architectural/maintainability risk. Some of the explicit sets may also be redundant when the flow already uses `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`, though that redundancy cannot be proven for every cited site from the shown hunks alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Layering leak: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider depends on the protocol-mapper internal AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken (widened from package-private to public static, a source-compat change for mapper subclasses), and that method reads the ambient session.getContext().getClient() rather than the client whose token is being created, which could diverge (e.g., token-exchange target client) and bake a wrong token-type marker into the ID; the policy should live in its own concern taking the client explicitly

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() calling AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) to derive tokenType, and AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper was changed to expose this as a public static method that reads session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...). This creates a cross-component dependency (encoder -> protocol-mapper internals) and relies on the ambient session context client rather than a client passed/derived from clientSessionContext, which could lead to mismatched lightweight/regular markers if the session context client is not the same as the token’s client. The potential divergence scenario (e.g., token exchange) isn’t directly proven in this diff, so it’s more an architecture/concern issue than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId is a speculative decode path with no production caller (tests only), and the lazy 'refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' fallbacks in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut handle a scenario that cannot occur (providers are fixed at startup and postInit runs after all factories load) while side-effecting shared maps from read paths; trim until needed or wire the consumer immediately

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new SPI (TokenContextEncoderProvider) and implements decoding via DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId, but within this PR the only visible caller of that decode API is the new unit test (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest). Production code shown (TokenManager.initToken) only encodes token IDs. Also, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut perform lazy “refresh” lookups and mutate the shared ConcurrentHashMaps from these read/lookup paths, even though postInit already eagerly populates the maps from provider factories; whether runtime deployment can happen isn’t proven from the diff, but the side-effecting fallback logic is a concrete architecture/complexity concern introduced here rather than a direct correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth2GrantType.setFormParams replaces this.formParams without re-deriving grantType (captured once in the constructor), leaving the context internally inconsistent with a stale or null grantType alongside fresh params; derive grantType lazily or update it in the setter

adjudication.rationale: In OAuth2GrantType.Context, a new field `grantType` is derived once in the constructor via `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`, and a getter `getGrantType()` is added. The existing `setFormParams(...)` remains (only its signature is visible in the diff) and there is no shown logic to recompute `grantType` when form params are replaced. This can leave `Context` with updated `formParams` but a stale/null `grantType` value, which is a real consistency concern introduced by caching grantType rather than deriving it on demand.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of the public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) is a silent source-compat break for external grant-type extensions that copied contexts, even though no in-repo callers remain; worth a release-notes mention or a deprecated-then-removed cycle

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previously existing copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` from `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context` (it is present in the removed block and no longer exists after the change). Since it was public API, this is a source-compatibility break for any external OAuth2 grant implementations/extensions that relied on copying the Context, even if there are no in-repo callers. This is an API/release-notes concern rather than an immediate runtime defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Magic string 'na' (UNKNOWN) conflates the encoded 2-char shortcut with the decoded grant-type domain value: AccessTokenContext.getGrantType() returns the literal 'na' when the grant was unrecorded, forcing callers to compare against the encoder impl's constant to detect unknown; use a sentinel on AccessTokenContext or a nullable grantType to keep the wire format out of the domain model

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a hardcoded UNKNOWN value `"na"` in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN`, and when the grant type is missing/unavailable the provider sets `grantType = UNKNOWN` and constructs `new AccessTokenContext(..., grantType, ...)` (both in `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` and `getTokenContextFromTokenId` for legacy token IDs). That means `AccessTokenContext.getGrantType()` can return the literal wire/sentinel value `"na"`, and the factory also maps `"na"` <-> `"na"` for encoding/decoding. Callers wanting to detect “unknown” must compare against this magic string (or the provider constant), so the finding’s concern about leaking wire-format/sentinel into the domain model is grounded in the diff. It’s an API/design issue rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId test matcher in AssertEvents.java (line 483) uses wrong substring offsets: the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5 of the encoded ID (e.g. 'onrtac:...'), so substring(3, 5) should be substring(4, 6); the current code extracts the 2nd char of the token-type shortcut plus the 1st char of the grant shortcut (e.g. 'ta' for 'onrtac')

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the encoded token-id prefix is 6 chars: 2(sessionType)+2(tokenType)+2(grantShortcut) as produced by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(). Therefore the grant shortcut is at indices [4,6) (e.g., "onrtac" -> "ac"). The matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which yields the last char of tokenType + first char of grant ("ta"), so it will mis-validate token IDs. Additionally, the condition is inverted: it returns false when the extracted substring equals expectedGrantShortcut.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId test matcher has inverted polarity: it returns false (matcher fails) when the extracted pair equals the expected grant shortcut and proceeds to the UUID check when it does not, which is exactly backwards

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, matchesSafely() returns false when the extracted grant shortcut equals expectedGrantShortcut: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` which inverts the intended logic. It should fail when it does NOT equal the expected shortcut, then proceed to UUID validation. Additionally, given the encoded layout (2 chars sessionType + 2 chars tokenType + 2 chars grantType), the grant shortcut should be at indices [4,6), not substring(3,5). As written, the matcher will reject correctly encoded token IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Net effect of the matcher bugs: isAccessTokenId degenerates to a 'one colon + UUID tail' check that passes regardless of which grant shortcut the encoder emitted, so the four updated expectations (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) verify none of the per-grant encoding and a regression emitting wrong grant shortcuts stays green (silent-pass guard)

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the grant-shortcut check is broken in two ways: (1) it uses items[0].substring(3, 5) even though the encoded context is 6 chars with grant shortcut in positions 4..6 (0-based), so substring(3,5) extracts the last char of tokenType + first char of grant (e.g., "onrtac" -> "ta"), which will almost never equal the expected grant shortcut; (2) the equality condition is inverted: `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Net effect is the matcher usually ignores the grant shortcut entirely and reduces to `one colon + UUID tail` (and would even fail when the extracted substring happens to equal the expected shortcut). This means the updated event expectations do not reliably validate per-grant encoding and can silently pass with wrong shortcuts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Latent spurious-failure in isAccessTokenId: an expected 'rt' shortcut matches chars 3-4 of a regular token ID from the token-exchange grant ('onrtte:...' -> 'rt'), causing false negatives

adjudication.rationale: `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` is implemented incorrectly. It extracts the grant shortcut using `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, but the encoder formats IDs as 6 chars before ':' (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grantType), so the grant shortcut should be at indices 4–6, not 3–5. Additionally, the matcher logic is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when the expected shortcut matches, guaranteeing false negatives for correctly-encoded IDs. This is a real defect introduced by the diff (tests expecting `isAccessTokenId(...)` would fail / matcher misbehaves).

adjudication_records.issue_text: substring(3, 5) in isAccessTokenId throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for any ID prefix shorter than 5 chars

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), after checking `items.length != 2`, it unconditionally calls `items[0].substring(3, 5)`. If the prefix part before ':' is shorter than 5 characters, this will throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of simply returning `false`, making the matcher unsafe for malformed/unexpected token IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Grant-shortcut contract mismatch: getShortcut() javadoc invites a '3-letters shortcut' but the decoder (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:76) hard-requires a 6-char context (2+2+2) and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise; all built-in shortcuts are 2 chars so the mismatch is invisible to in-repo tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() with Javadoc suggesting a “3-letters shortcut”, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() hard-requires the encoded context prefix length to be exactly 6 chars (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grantType) and throws IllegalArgumentException if not ("Expected length of 6."). encodeTokenId() concatenates the grant shortcut without enforcing its length, so any grant implementation returning a 3-char shortcut (as encouraged by the Javadoc) will produce token IDs that cannot be decoded by this implementation. In-repo grants use 2-char shortcuts (ac/rt/cc/...), so tests won’t catch it, but the contract mismatch is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: encodeTokenId (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:105-118) performs no length, charset, or collision validation of the shortcut: a custom grant factory following the javadoc (e.g. 'abc') produces IDs like 'onrtabc:uuid' that encode successfully but can never be decoded (encode/decode asymmetry surfacing at decode time), and a shortcut containing ':' corrupts the colon-split entirely

adjudication.rationale: The new token ID encoding/decoding scheme hard-codes a 2-char grant shortcut but does not validate it. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)` concatenates `sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grantShort+':'+rawId` with no checks on `grantShort`, while `getTokenContextFromTokenId(...)` enforces `encodedContext.length() == 6` and slices grant shortcut as `substring(4,6)`. Any custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` longer/shorter than 2 chars (the javadoc even suggests “3-letters shortcut”) will encode successfully but fail decoding (IllegalArgumentException). Additionally, if a shortcut contains ':' the decoder’s `indexOf(':')` split breaks, corrupting parsing. This is an encode/decode correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: postInit duplicate-shortcut validation is only a size comparison (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()), which detects some but not all shortcut collisions

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), duplicate detection only checks whether grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size(). This can miss real collisions when duplicates in IDs and shortcuts “cancel out” so both maps end up with the same size (e.g., (id1,s1),(id1,s2),(id2,s2) -> both maps size 2). In such cases, the maps are not a bijection and encoding/decoding token IDs can become ambiguous/incorrect, but the validation would not throw.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lazy registration paths in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:110-137) put into the shared maps with no collision check, bypassing postInit validation entirely; a lazily registered colliding shortcut silently overwrites the previous mapping, so previously issued tokens decode as the wrong grant type

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, the lazy refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() update the shared maps via plain put(...) (e.g., grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) / grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut)) with no collision/consistency check. This bypasses the postInit duplicate-shortcut validation (which only checks sizes right after initial population). If a newly deployed OAuth2GrantTypeFactory reports a shortcut already in use, the existing shortcut->grant mapping can be silently overwritten, causing previously issued token IDs using that shortcut to decode to the wrong grant type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext constructor (lines 79-80) has a copy-pasted requireNonNull: the second line checks grantType again instead of rawTokenId, so rawTokenId is never null-checked; a null rawTokenId flows through and yields token IDs like 'onrtna:null'

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added AccessTokenContext constructor, the last null-check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This is a copy/paste error visible in the diff, so `rawTokenId` is not null-validated and could propagate; `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which would yield `...:null` if `rawTokenId` is null.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testIncorrectGrantType (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:95-104) passes via incidental NPE rather than the intended validation: the test factory never runs postInit so sessionFactory is null and decoding 'ofrtac:5678' NPEs inside getGrantTypeByShortcut; even if the shortcut validation were deleted the test would still pass (NPE from requireNonNull(grantType) in AccessTokenContext), and catch(RuntimeException) swallows both, so the test cannot detect removal of the decode validation

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the new test `testIncorrectGrantType` catches any `RuntimeException` and does not assert the specific failure mode. In `before()`, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` never has `postInit()` invoked, so `sessionFactory` remains null. When decoding `"ofrtac:5678"`, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId()` calls `factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut("ac")`; since the shortcut is absent from `grantsByShortcuts`, `getGrantTypeByShortcut` attempts `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`, which will NPE with null `sessionFactory`. That NPE is swallowed by the broad catch, so the test can pass incidentally rather than verifying the intended validation/exception behavior.
